articles.title: Electron vs Tauri: how to choose for your next desktop app
articles.excerpt: If you want to build a desktop app with web technology, you'll end up choosing between Electron and Tauri. Both let you write the interface in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with React, Svelte, Vue, or wh…
articles.body: If you want to build a desktop app with web technology, you'll end up choosing between Electron and Tauri . Both let you write the interface in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with React, Svelte, Vue, or whatever you already use. The difference is everything underneath it. I've built and shipped desktop apps with both. Here are the differences that actually mattered, and how I'd decide today. The one-line version Electron ships a browser with your app. Tauri borrows the one the operating system already has. An Electron app bundles its own copy of Chromium to draw the interface, and Node.js to run the backend. A Tauri app uses the system webview (WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on macOS and Linux) and runs its backend in Rust, compiled into one small native binary.

Some of them simply asked: "Is this project alive?" It is. Here is what happened, what changed, and how to upgrade. Why it stopped There was no big drama. articles.body: I build an Android camera that tells you which way to move the phone. You tap a detail, the app follows it, and a ring turns green when that detail sits on a composition guide and the phone is ready. This post covers the parts that were harder than they looked: following a tapped patch of pixels, bridging fast turns with the gyroscope, and refusing to let any estimate produce the green state. Spiralens screenshot by the author, taken on the Android emulator's virtual scene (a rendered room, not a real photo). Why not object detection The user decides what the subject is. A mug, a dog's eye, a doorway: a detector would need a class for each. So the tracker follows whatever patch was tapped.

It works for stores of every size, from small shops to large enterprise retailers, and has kept adding features as merchant needs have grown more complex. Despite these strengths, Magento has traditionally struggled with frontend performance. Its default frontend relies on a heavy JavaScript stack, including RequireJS, Knockout.js, jQuery, and LESS. Even merchants who invest heavily in performance optimization often struggle to hit strong Core Web Vitals and PageSpeed scores, simply because of how the default frontend is built. Hyvä built the Hyvä Theme to replace Magento’s default frontend.

articles.title: Building a Free IQ Test Site: What Goes Into Scoring
articles.excerpt: When I set out to build IQCognify, I thought the hard part would be the questions. It wasn't. Writing pattern-recognition and logic puzzles is fun. The hard part was everything around them: making the…
articles.body: When I set out to build IQCognify, I thought the hard part would be the questions. It wasn't. Writing pattern-recognition and logic puzzles is fun. The hard part was everything around them: making the test fair, making the score mean something, and making the whole thing run fast in a browser with no signup wall. The score has to mean something An IQ score only works because it is normalized. By definition, 100 is the average, and the scale uses a standard deviation of 15. That means a score of 115 is one standard deviation above average, 130 is two. If your scoring is sloppy — if the questions are too easy, or the mix is unbalanced — the numbers stop meaning anything.

articles.title: Why we built voice AI for the device, not the cloud
articles.excerpt: The default is to send voice to the cloud If you are shipping a voice feature in your app today, odds are you are sending audio to a server. That is how most existing solutions work. The mobile app ca…
articles.body: The default is to send voice to the cloud If you are shipping a voice feature in your app today, odds are you are sending audio to a server. That is how most existing solutions work. The mobile app captures sound from the microphone, packages it as WAV or opus, streams it to an API endpoint, and gets back JSON with the recognized text. Your business logic then operates on text. This pattern dominates not because it is the best approach, but because historically it was the only one that worked at real production model sizes. Open ASR models were too big. On-device model quality was noticeably worse than the cloud equivalents. Mobile hardware could not sustain ML inference in the background without destroying battery life inside an hour. The trade-off did not satisfy us for very long.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo’s hinge cooling is the breakthrough Android foldables need
articles.excerpt: Android foldables typically do not use the hinge as part of the thermal dissipation layer.
articles.body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple built a flexible graphite pipe into the iPhone Duo hinge to dissipate excess heat between the two chassis halves when folded. Combined with an unstacked A20 Pro SoC and vapor chamber, the active thermal hinge helps maintain peak performance for longer under heavy loads. Android foldables have used graphite sheets as part of the display stack or on the chassis on either side of the spine, but have not typically used the spine itself for cooling. Foldables have spent years balancing thinner profiles with flagship-grade SoCs and the resulting thermal dilemma.

articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched 27 of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 12), the first such mission for a Falcon 9 rocket since Sept. 19.
articles.body: SpaceX just broke an uncharacteristically long Starlink launch drought. The company sent 27 of its Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) today (Oct. 12), launching them atop a Falcon 9 rocket from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:28 p.m. EDT (5:28 p.m. local time; 0028 GMT on Oct. 13) It was the first Starlink mission for a Falcon 9 since Sept. 19 , which was another 27-satellite liftoff from Vandenberg. For some perspective on this recent gap: Between Aug. 19 and Sept. 6, a span of 19 days, SpaceX launched seven Starlink missions with Falcon 9s. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a ship at sea shortly after the Oct. 12 launch. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX did loft a batch of Starlinks after that, but it wasn't aboard a Falcon 9.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.

articles.title: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Mission to Launch Health Research
articles.excerpt: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency…
articles.body: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, advancing research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration. This research supports astronaut health during long-duration missions through four investigations from the agency’s Biological and Physical Sciences division, including 3D models of the human brain, a crop disease study, a faster way to assess astronaut health, and an analysis of antibiotic-resistant bacteria aboard the space station.

articles.body: Friday, October 16, 2026 Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Join senior AI reporter James O’Donnell as he interviews King about his work, being named one of MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35 and new ways of seeing biology.
